sermon.title: Last Day to Live Part 2
sermon.speaker: Pastor Kincer
sermon.summary: Daniel refused rewards and reminded Belshazzar that God holds his breath. Like Felix, he knew but didn’t act. God sends warnings to turn people back. Belshazzar was weighed and found wanting and died that night. A small righteous minority, like the abolitionists, can change a nation.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then Daniel answered, and said before the king, “Let your gifts be for yourself, and give your rewards to another; yet I will read the writing to the king, and make known to him the interpretation. O king, the Most High God gave Nebuchadnezzar your father a kingdom and majesty, glory and honor. And because of the majesty that He gave him, all peoples, nations, and languages trembled and feared before him. Whomever he wished, he executed; whomever he wished, he kept alive; whomever he wished, he set up; and whomever he wished, he put down. But when his heart was lifted up, and his spirit was hardened in pride, he was deposed from his kingly throne, and they took his glory from him. Then he was driven from the sons of men, his heart was made like the beasts, and his dwelling was with the wild donkeys. They fed him with grass like oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven, till he knew that the Most High God rules in the kingdom of men, and appoints over it whomever He chooses. “But you his son, Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart, although you knew all this. And you have lifted yourself up against the Lord of heaven. They have brought the vessels of His house before you, and you and your lords, your wives and your concubines, have drunk wine from them. And you have praised the gods of silver and gold, bronze and iron, wood and stone, which do not see or hear or know; and the God who holds your breath in His hand and owns all your ways, you have not glorified.

How many know we need to move on to Christianity? We need to get through our faith and our belief and move on to following Jesus Christ. There are many people in America who believe and are not followers. You know them by their fruits or their faith? Fruits. Isn’t that beautiful? Now, look. Many people fear. When the scriptures are being preached, when they read the scriptures, and God comes to them, they fear God, but they won’t follow.

Look at this account. Acts 24:25. As Paul reasoned to Felix, now here is the message that needs to get out. We gave you the three responses. Here is the three truths that you need to preach to be getting the full gospel out. Do you understand me? You young adults, this is your outline of how to get the word of God out. Now, Paul’s standing before a civil leader. He didn’t flatter that civil leader. He didn’t approve of that civil leader. He confronted that civil leader with three things. Are you ready, church? Paul reasoned. What does the atheist use and homosexual and all that?

What’s their word? Reason, logical thinking. He taught Paul Felix some logical things from the Bible. Righteousness. He said, “Felix, you got to live right. You got to speak right. You got to do right.” Number two, he said, “Felix, you got to use temperance or self-control.” Oh, but us Pentecostals, we want the Holy Ghost just to do it. No, you got to use self-control. You got to control yourself. You got to say no to sexual immorality. You got to say no to lying. You got to say no to intoxication. You got to say no. You’ve got to control yourself, discipline yourself.

Amen. And then he said, “Felix, there’s a judgment coming. If you don’t live right, if you don’t control yourself, you’re going to be punished in that judgment.” You young adults, did you get this? You leaders coming up in this church, do you understand this? When you’re out there getting the message out, you got to incorporate these three things. If you want people’s hearts to be pricked, you want their spirit to be shaken, it says Felix trembled. Here’s that fear again. Righteousness, self-control, and a punishment if you don’t do it.

That’s Bible morality. Now, Daniel interprets the writing and deals with both the kingdom and the individual. Part of the hand with writing from him, they saw the hand many many Tekel Upharsin. That’s the writing. Daniel tells him this is the writing. Here is the interpretation. God has numbered your kingdom and finished it. The kingdom, the nation is going to be dealt with. Secondly, Tekel, you’ve weighed and weighed in the balance and found lacking. The individual. God is going to judge you as an individual and you lack. You’re in trouble, friend. My friend, you are in trouble. Your kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and the Persians. Here he is. He said, “I’m going to turn the kingdom, the people over to another authority, a new king.” Now, how many want Jesus to be that new king?

chunks.short_answer: Weighed and found wanting—that night Belshazzar was slain.
chunks.text:
Have you got it? Now, he’s in there exalting himself, and this is what’s going on. It’s not only in the Bible, but it’s in history. It’s written in history. Okay? You see a picture here of Babylon. 300-ft walls, a moat all around it fed by the Euphrates River. Okay? Impregnable. No one had ever conquered the city of Babylon. They had such security. They had such confidence that they were okay. Is Americans like that? Oh, yeah. We think because of our atomic bombs and our, you know, aircraft carriers and our military, you know, with it, man, we’re just solid. Let me tell you, when God brings the hammer down, there’s nothing that can keep Salvador from overrunning America.

You say that’s a little extreme. Well, now here is a top view pictorial of Babylon. You see the Euphrates River running through the city? They had an endless supply of water. Wasn’t polluted like it is today. Endless supply water. They had hanging gardens. They could grow their own They could maintain for a long time. They could maintain a siege. They were so confident, cocky, they No one could get into that city. But Cyrus immediately got his engineers to start digging a channel, a low place in the land to divert part of the Euphrates River. And he ignited that diversion the night Belshazzar went through his last day on Earth.

And the Euphrates River went down to shallow water, the military waited through that water at both ends, both this end and this end. And they took the city without hardly a shot fired. Why? Because they were in a festival. They were bragging about how they were safe and they had false confidence and they can’t come in here. And there they were. Instantly Belshazzar was killed.
